site.name: Morning Star Mine
site.componentDetail: Named underground lead-silver mine associated with the Morning Star Mining Company and McHarg shaft on Carbonate Hill
overview: Morning Star Mine is a documented historic underground mine on Leadville’s Carbonate Hill. U.S. Geological Survey reports identify the Morning Star Mining Company, its McHarg shaft operations, and underground connections in the surrounding mine network.
The mine is best understood as one component of the densely interconnected Carbonate Hill workings rather than as an isolated surface feature.

timeline.text: The Morning Star Mining Company operated underground workings on Carbonate Hill through the McHarg shaft.
USGS documentation records connections between Morning Star workings and neighboring mine systems, including the Henriette.
Federal geological studies continued to identify the Morning Star or Evening Star mine within the Leadville district.

moreHistory: USGS Professional Paper 138 documents Morning Star Mining Company operations and the McHarg shaft in the Carbonate Hill area.
USGS Professional Paper 561 independently identifies the Morning Star or Evening Star mine in the district’s geologic context.
Remnant does not present unsupported production totals or imply that historic underground workings are accessible.
